chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Doc Cook, doctor of music and his Seventeen Interns
summary: Zutty laughs that he still talked with Doc Cook about the bass drum on Broadway; Cook held a music doctorate and led Doc Cook and His Seventeen Interns.

bands.name: Doc Cook and His Seventeen Interns

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Good musician. Well he had to be to play in Charlie Cook's band. That bass drum deal, that was the thing because I would see Charlie Cook on Broadway every now and then see, and we'd talk about it you know. (LAUGHTER).
It would be funny years later.
Because he was really a doctor of music you know. Doc Cook and his Seventeen Interns, that was the name of the band.
He got a degree in music.
Doctor of music. Sure was so fine, so high class. Nice, you know. Just lovely.
